identity.title: Do as We Do, Not as You Think: the Conformity of Large Language Models

problem.claim: The paper studies conformity in LLM-driven multi-agent collaboration, including its existence, influencing factors, and mitigation strategies.

gap.claim: Conformity in LLM multi-agent systems remains largely unexplored, creating concerns about collective problem solving and ethical implications.

contributions.claim: Introduces BenchForm, a conformity-oriented benchmark with reasoning-intensive tasks and five interaction protocols for probing collaborative behavior.
Evaluates representative LLMs with conformity rate and independence rate, and analyzes interaction time, majority size, and rationalizations of conforming behavior.
Explores enhanced personas and a reflection mechanism as approaches to mitigate conformity effects.

stated_novelty.claim: BenchForm is presented as a new benchmark specifically oriented toward conformity in collaborative LLM scenarios.

narrative_sequence.summary: LLMs enable collaborative multi-agent systems, but conformity analogous to human conformity bias and group-think is largely unexplored.
The study examines conformity’s existence, influencing factors, and possible mitigation.
BenchForm combines reasoning-intensive tasks with five interaction protocols; representative LLMs are evaluated using conformity and independence rates.
The paper examines interaction time, majority size, and conforming rationalizations, then explores enhanced personas and reflection.
The benchmark and code are reported as available at BenchForm.

source_observation.claim: The study pairs a purpose-built benchmark and multiple interaction protocols with explicit conformity and independence metrics.

lessons.interpretation: This links the measurement design to the behavioral phenomenon under study and exposes protocol-dependent collaboration effects.
lessons.application: For a behavioral claim, define task conditions, interaction variants, and metrics that directly operationalize both the target behavior and its complement.
lessons.exception: This design may be unsuitable when the behavior cannot be isolated with reliable operational metrics or when protocol variation is not part of the research question.

unknowns: The abstract does not report the direction or magnitude of conformity findings, effects of interaction time or majority size, mitigation outcomes, or case-study details.
The abstract does not specify BenchForm’s task contents, evaluated model identities, metric definitions, or the location/access details behind “BenchForm.”
